sections.h2: Where is the Montmorency County register of deeds?
sections.html:
The Montmorency County register of deeds is in Atlanta, the county seat, at 12265 M-32 West, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 789, Atlanta, MI 49709. The phone number is 989-785-8079. The county site lists weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and says the office stays open through the lunch hour.

The office is the official recorder for every legal instrument that transfers or encumbers land in the county, and it records mineral interests as well as surface interests. Staff check each document against Michigan's recording rules before accepting it, then scan the original, index it by grantor and grantee and add it to a tract index that lets anyone search by legal description.

The same office chairs the county plat board, takes passport applications and keeps copies of recorded documents for the public. Title companies, abstractors, attorneys, oil and gas land agents and township assessors all rely on it.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Montmorency County itself?
sections.html:
Montmorency County lies in Northern Michigan in the Lake Huron watershed, with the Thunder Bay River draining much of it toward Alpena. It spans 563 square miles, of which 547 are land, and most of that land is state forest. The Legislature created it in 1840 under another name, renamed it in 1843 and organized it in 1881. Atlanta became the seat in 1891.

The county had 9,153 residents in the 2020 census, which makes it the second-least populous county in the Lower Peninsula. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 9,842, up 7.5% since 2020. About 35.4% of residents are 65 or older, and households average 1.92 people.

Housing here has its own shape. The 2020 census counted 8,930 housing units and found 51.6% of them vacant, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 8,933 units. Tourism-related services and retail form most of the economic base, with dairy and dry beans in farming, and ORV and snowmobile trails run through the county. Owners live in 87.9% of the occupied homes.

  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $158,600.
  • Median household income: $49,756.
  • Median gross rent: $686.
  • Building permits in 2025, per the Census Bureau: 0.

Townships include Albert, Avery, Briley, Hillman, Loud, Montmorency, Rust and Vienna, plus the Village of Hillman. Name the township on any listing or deed, since its assessor handles your tax records.

sections.h2: What does the Montmorency County register of deeds record?
sections.html:
Besides deeds and mortgages, the county page offers forms for a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, an affidavit of affixture of a mobile home, a notice of intention to maintain mineral rights and a principal residence exemption. It also links schedules for statutory fees, copy and search fees, uniform commercial code fees, recording requirements and transfer tax.

For a cabin or hunting parcel, three document types come up often.

  • A deed that carries the exact legal description, since a tract index search runs on that description.
  • A survey recorded with the office, when a boundary matters to the buyer. The county page lists several surveyors and independent searchers in the region.
  • The affidavit or notice that applies to a mobile home or to mineral rights, if either sits in your chain of title.

Buyers of northern Michigan recreation property often want to know what sits under and around the land, so the register's tract index is the first stop for easements, leases and recorded plats.

The county also lists title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord. A title company can prepare the deed and order the search the buyer will want, and the register's staff cannot do that work for you.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Montmorency County?
sections.html:
State law sets $30.00 per document as the recording fee, regardless of page count, under MCL 600.2567. A document assigning or discharging more than one instrument adds $3.00 per additional instrument. Copies cost $1.00 per page, a certified copy adds $5.00 and a records search runs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 minimum.

Fees are due when the document is left. A charter county may use a different schedule, so open the county's statutory fee sheet or call 989-785-8079 before you send a check.

Recorded paper must follow MCL 565.201: black ink on white paper, 10-point type, a 2.5-inch blank top margin on page one, the drafter's name and address and a first line that names the recordable event. A Social Security number must have its first five digits removed.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will a Montmorency County seller owe?
sections.html:
The seller pays two taxes at recording: $3.75 per $500 to the state and $0.55 per $500 to the county, each rounded up to the next $500. Payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed. Using the county median value gives a sense of scale.

A deed for less than $100 in consideration, a land contract that does not pass title until it is paid in full and a transfer made to confirm title already held, such as a corrective quitclaim, escape both taxes. The exemption belongs on the face of the deed. Where a seller owns the same parcel across a county line, the sale price is split and tax goes to each county.

sections.h2: Which property tax steps follow a sale in Montmorency County?
sections.html:
The buyer must report the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days on the state form, giving the parties, date, price and parcel number. Under MCL 211.27a, a transfer of ownership lets the next year's taxable value rise to the state equalized value, which is set at 50% of true cash value. Transfers of residential property to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild who does not use it commercially are among the exceptions.

If the seller claimed the principal residence exemption, a Request to Rescind (Form 2602) goes to the assessor within 90 days after the house stops being the owner's home. The penalty for filing late is $5 a day to a maximum of $200, and the exemption comes off on December 31. A buyer who will live in the home files Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1 to start the exemption for the summer or winter bill.

Ask the Montmorency County treasurer for the status of the parcel's taxes before closing. Sellers of recreational property should also ask the township assessor which taxable value the parcel carries today, because a cabin held for many years usually has a taxable value well under the state equalized value that a new owner will see after the transfer.

A seller who inherited the property should remember that a conveyance by will or intestate succession counts as a transfer of ownership unless the heir is the surviving spouse or a listed close relative taking residential property that stays non-commercial. The assessor can confirm which rule fits.

faqs.q: What hours does the Montmorency County register of deeds keep?
faqs.a: The county site lists Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and says the office is open during lunch. Call 989-785-8079 to check holiday closings.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a $158,600 sale?
faqs.a: It is $1,367.40, made up of $1,192.50 for the state and $174.90 for the county. The seller pays it, and the price rounds up to the next $500 before the rates apply.

faqs.q: Does the office draft a deed for me?
faqs.a: No. The office records documents and keeps indexes. The county page offers quit claim and warranty deed forms, but a title company or attorney should confirm the form fits your situation.

faqs.q: Do mineral rights transfer with my deed?
faqs.a: Check the chain of title. The register records mineral interests separately from surface interests, and the office lists a notice form for maintaining mineral rights. A title company can tell you whether any were severed from your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to give up my principal residence exemption after a sale?
faqs.a: Ninety days after the property stops being your principal residence. File Form 2602 with the township assessor. Late filing costs $5 a day up to $200.
